channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits and Preferences for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A seminar in Surkhandarya discussed a presidential decree offering new benefits for entrepreneurs, including a three-year exemption from inspections for small businesses. The decree also introduces economic amnesty for small and medium enterprises and allows independent audits for larger businesses, aiming to reduce state intervention and protect business activities.

item.title: CIS Interpol National Bureaus Discuss Cooperation Development in Minsk
item.description: Heads of Interpol National Central Bureaus (NCBs) from CIS member states met in Minsk to discuss cooperation. Delegations from Azerbaijan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, UAE, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on enhancing international law enforcement cooperation, information exchange, and addressing existing challenges.

item.title: Russian budget received 321 billion rubles from migration processes
item.description: President Vladimir Putin stated that migration processes generated 321 billion rubles in revenue for Russia over 18 months. Over 60 billion rubles went to the federal budget, and more than 250-260 billion rubles to regional budgets. The Interior Ministry reported expelling approximately 100,000 migrants for violations, with 75,000 deported forcibly.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes land transfer to state for non-residential property sales to foreigners
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering new rules for selling non-residential real estate to foreign citizens. If the land plot of a property is privately owned by the seller, it must be transferred to state or municipal ownership for free to finalize the sale. The draft law is open for public discussion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan showcases investment potential at China's CIFIT international fair
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's investment potential was presented at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen. The National Investment Agency highlighted promising sectors and opportunities for joint projects. Participation aims to attract foreign capital and expand business contacts with international investors.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces criminal liability for illegal underground tunnels across border
item.description: Uzbekistan is introducing criminal liability for the construction and use of illegal underground tunnels across the state border, as well as for organizing and financing such activities. The Senate approved amendments to the Criminal and Criminal Procedure Codes. Since 2016, 12 such tunnels have been discovered.

item.title: Russian Strikes Hit Sumy and Mykolaiv Regions, Causing Casualties
item.description: Russian forces conducted new strikes on Sumy and Mykolaiv regions on September 10, 2026, resulting in fatalities and injuries. Attacks on Sumy killed two young people, with around 20 injured. Mykolaiv region's port infrastructure was hit, killing two and injuring at least 12, including a toddler.

item.title: Uzbekistan Welcomed 9.1 Million Tourists in Eight Months
item.description: From January to August 2026, Uzbekistan hosted 9.1 million foreign tourists, a 21.1% increase from the previous year. August alone saw nearly 1.5 million visitors. Tourism revenue reached $4.6 billion, a 53.5% rise, with significant growth from Asian, US, and Russian travelers.

item.title: Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Glaciers Show 1.5-2 Meter Decline
item.description: An international expedition in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region recorded a 1.5-2 meter decline in glaciers Zoulmart, No. 3, and No. 457 in August 2026. The research, involving Swiss universities, aims to study glacier dynamics as indicators of climate change.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans International Logistics Center in Sary-Tash
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to establish an international transport and logistics center in Sary-Tash, potentially attracting up to $100 million in investment. The center will be part of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan-Afghanistan corridor, aiming to boost transit, trade, and job creation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan establishes center to streamline foreign student admissions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has created a state enterprise, 'Center for Admission of Foreign Students,' to make the process more transparent and attract more international applicants. The number of foreign students in the country has decreased significantly in recent years. The center aims to centralize recruitment, document verification, and student support.

item.title: Bishkek court deliberates on 'Letter of 75' case verdict
item.description: The Bishkek City Court has retired to chambers to issue a verdict in the 'Letter of 75' case. Previously, the Pervomaisky District Court sentenced several former officials, including Kamchybek Tashiev, to four years imprisonment with probation. Both the prosecution and defense appealed this sentence.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Inclusive Education Challenges and Teacher Preparedness
item.description: Uzbekistan has over 132,000 school-aged children with disabilities. While 6,801 children are included in inclusive education, 17,056 receive home-based learning. Experts discuss the definition of inclusive education, teacher readiness, and the balance between reform speed and quality.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Meet in Minsk to Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS countries met in Minsk on September 9, 2026, to discuss international cooperation and information exchange. Representatives from Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan participated. Observers from Interpol General Secretariat and the UAE also attended.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Manager of Tashkent International Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, has been appointed as the manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center on a concurrent basis with her current position.

item.title: Uzbek Alphabet Reform: Proposals for Keyboard Layout of New Letters
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to adapt state information systems to the new Latin alphabet, including letters Ö, Ğ, Ş, and Ç. The Ministry of Digital Technologies is developing technical standards for integration, data migration, and document circulation, potentially placing new letters on separate keys.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Manager of Tashkent International Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, has been appointed as the manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center. In this role, she will coordinate the center's operations, prepare initial documents, and foster cooperation between state bodies and the center's structures. She will also represent the center internationally and participate in personnel decisions.

item.title: UN Expert Calls for Protection of Elderly Rights Regardless of Age or Diagnosis
item.description: An independent UN expert urges a new approach to protecting the rights of the elderly, citing global population aging and cognitive impairments. He emphasizes that cognitive decline does not diminish a person's dignity or fundamental rights. The expert warns against ageism and decisions made for the elderly without considering their will.

item.title: Criminal Liability for Illegal Tunnels at Uzbekistan Border to Be Introduced
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish specific criminal liability for constructing illegal tunnels across its border. Over the past decade, 12 illegal underground structures and tunnels were identified. The Senate approved a law imposing stricter penalties for those using them to cross the border or smuggle goods.

item.title: Tajikistan Strengthens Counter-Terrorism Cooperation Amidst Globalization Challenges
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Interior Minister attended international events in China focusing on combating terrorism, extremism, and transnational crime. The conference emphasized the global nature of these threats and the need for enhanced international cooperation. Participants discussed new security challenges and the importance of digital methods for crime prevention and counteraction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Defendant in Power Seizure Case Requests Open Trial from President
item.description: Temirlan Sultanbekov, on trial for an alleged attempt to seize power, has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for a public trial. Having spent significant time in detention, he argues an open trial would demonstrate the fairness of the investigation and judicial process. He states he seeks nothing for himself, only justice.

item.title: Over 96,000 Uzbek Citizens Returned from Russia in 10 Days
item.description: More than 96,000 Uzbek citizens have returned to Uzbekistan from Russia in the past 10 days. Over 54,000 came directly from Russia, while the rest transited through Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to citizens facing difficult situations.

item.title: All Uzbek school textbooks to transition to new alphabet by 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to fully transition all school textbooks to the updated Uzbek alphabet between 2027 and 2031. The Deputy Minister of Preschool and School Education stated that textbooks for first graders will use the new alphabet starting in 2027, with all textbooks updated by 2031.

item.title: Five arrested at Namangan airport attempting to smuggle gold worth $1.1 billion to India
item.description: Five individuals were apprehended at Namangan International Airport for attempting to illegally export gold worth 1.1 billion soums to India. The suspects, from Andijan and Fergana regions, were using their bodies as 'live containers' to smuggle 555 grams of gold bars and 200 grams of jewelry.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves New 28-Letter Latin-Based Alphabet Variant
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan approved a new variant of the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet, consisting of 28 letters and one apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three digraphs. The proposed reform aims to align the writing system with the "one sound - one letter" principle and address issues with digital usage. The bill now moves to the president for review.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Showcases First Robotic Surgery System at Medical Academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's first robotic surgery system was unveiled at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. The Ministry of Health reported that the robot assists surgeons by enabling precise instrument control and magnified views through small incisions, enhancing complex operations.

item.title: UzAuto Motors Launches First Chevrolet Hybrid Model, the Equinox PHEV
item.description: UzAuto Motors has announced the launch of its first hybrid model, the Chevrolet Equinox PHEV crossover. Available in two trims, the vehicle features a plug-in hybrid system allowing short trips on electric power alone, with a total range exceeding 1000 km.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election Date Set for January 27, 2027, Parliament to Confirm
item.description: The Zhogorku Kenesh (parliament) is expected to officially set the presidential election date for January 27, 2027, on September 24. The Central Election Commission stated that the election will proceed on this date regardless of parliamentary resolution, with campaigning to begin in December.

item.title: Uzbekistan Privatizes State Assets Worth Over $8 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's President has approved a large-scale privatization program, putting state assets worth approximately $8 billion up for auction. The program includes stakes in 84 companies, 1,242 real estate objects, and 8,000 hectares of land. Major assets like Turonbank and Humo Air are included, with plans to liquidate or reorganize 85 state-owned enterprises.

item.title: GKNB uncovers state damage in purchase of two combine harvesters in Naryn region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has identified state damage amounting to 4.945 million soms during the procurement of two combine harvesters in the Min-Bulak rural district of Naryn region. Criminal proceedings are underway to investigate the actions of involved officials and recover the losses.

item.title: Imprisoned politician Temirlan Sultanbekov writes letter to Kyrgyzstan's president
item.description: Imprisoned politician Temirlan Sultanbekov has written a letter to President Sadyr Japarov from pre-trial detention center SIZO-1. Sultanbekov stated he would not ask for mercy, emphasizing his commitment to the 'Kyrgyz spirit,' and requested an open trial.

item.title: Russian scientists to study infections in Kyrgyzstan with population surveys
item.description: The St. Petersburg Pasteur Research Institute will organize population studies in Kyrgyzstan from October 16 to November 15, 2026. The research aims to study infections, involving the collection and laboratory testing of biological samples from 70 points across the country.

item.title: Sughd region plans to process waste into organic fertilizers
item.description: Officials in Tajikistan's Sughd region met with Iranian counterparts to discuss cooperation in waste management and recycling. Plans include updating sewage networks, reconstructing landfills, and implementing technologies to produce organic fertilizers from waste, potentially starting in Khujand.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Housing Market Sees 21% Growth in Seven Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's housing market experienced a 21% increase in sales during the first seven months of the year. The number of real estate transactions rose to 34,300. Sales growth was observed in most regions, with the highest figures recorded in the capital city.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan introduces first robotic surgical system at medical academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Medical Academy has unveiled the country's first robotic surgical system. The system enhances surgeon precision and visualization through small incisions, but the doctor remains in full control during operations. The academy plans to begin robot-assisted surgeries soon, with another system to be acquired for the National Center for Mother and Child Healthcare.

item.title: Two former police officers in Syrdarya sentenced to 5 and 6 years for bribery
item.description: Two former officers from the Khovos district police department in Syrdarya region were sentenced to five and six years in prison for demanding bribes. They were accused of fabricating evidence and extorting money from a farmer regarding a land dispute. The officers were apprehended while receiving part of the demanded sum.

item.title: Uzbek citizens returning from abroad can receive grants up to 60 million soums for business expansion
item.description: Uzbek citizens who worked abroad and returned to start businesses can receive grants up to 60 million soums to expand their ventures and create jobs. The program, a collaboration between the Migration Agency and IOM with Swedish funding, targets returnees from 2025-2026. Special support is given to women entrepreneurs.

item.title: Chinese Vice Premier Calls for Greater Openness in Services Trade
item.description: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang emphasized the need for greater openness and cooperation in the services trade sector, stating it's a global necessity. He proposed reducing barriers to cross-border factor movement and promoting liberalization to support socio-economic development.

item.title: Tajikistan Celebrates 35th Anniversary of Independence with Cultural Program
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a cultural program at the National Stadium to mark Tajikistan's 35th anniversary of independence. President Emomali Rahmon addressed the attendees, highlighting the importance of peace, stability, and national unity for the country's development and prosperity.

item.title: Parents of Children with SSPE Protest for Medical Aid and Support
item.description: Parents of children suffering from Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE), a severe complication of measles, gathered outside the Ministry of Health in Uzbekistan demanding essential medications, medical care, and financial assistance. The ministry reported approximately 350 children have SSPE, with 60 deaths.
